**Low confidence — these don't corroborate each other, and I can't resolve which is current from what you've pasted.**

Here's the actual conflict: the wiki gives an SLA number (200ms, p99, rolling 7-day window) — that's a specific, contractual-sounding commitment with a defined measurement method. The public docs give a looser figure (250ms, p99, "expect under") with no stated window. Those aren't the same kind of claim even before you get to the numbers disagreeing — one reads like an internal guarantee, the other reads like a customer-facing expectation-setter, and those two things are allowed to differ on purpose (docs teams often pad the public number so they're not constantly explaining SLA breaches). So this could be either (a) a real inconsistency where one page is stale, or (b) two intentionally different numbers that just look like a contradiction because neither page says so explicitly.

I can't tell which without more than what's in front of me — I don't have a way to pull either page's edit history myself right now. What would settle it:

- Last-modified date on both pages — if one's 18 months old, that's probably your answer.
- Who owns each doc — if the SLA number comes from whatever team writes actual contracts/support commitments, that's the one that matters legally regardless of what the public page says.
- Whether "expect under 250ms" is explicitly framed as a looser target than the SLA anywhere else in the public docs (a sentence like "typical performance" vs "guaranteed" would confirm it's intentional, not a stale copy-paste).

If you can grab me the last-edit dates or point me at whoever owns the SLA doc, I can turn this into an actual answer instead of a flagged discrepancy.
